rules.statement: When a boolean property or method such as `IsConfigured` guarantees that a nullable member is non-null when it returns true, annotate it with `[MemberNotNullWhen(true, nameof(Member))]` so callers can read the member directly after the check, without null-forgiving operators or a second null check.
rules.why: The maintainer asked for the not-null-when attribute so the compiler's nullable analysis knows the guard's guarantee, and callers can read the value directly once the guard is true.
rules.check: Look for nullable properties on options or other classes that sit next to a guard property or method that checks them. Report it when the guard has no `[MemberNotNullWhen]`/`[NotNullWhen]`, or when callers use `!` or check for null again after the guard.
